macros.name: ctrl
macros.doc: Starting point of a controlled gate, using filled circle (\ctrl) or open circle (\octrl).

macros.name: forceredefine
macros.doc: If you wish to ensure that you are using the version that this package defines, run \forceredefine at the end of your preamble (after all packages have loaded).

macros.name: gategroup
macros.doc: Create a large box with top-left-hand corner positioned (roughly) at the top-left of the current cell.

macros.name: hphantomgate
macros.doc: Places a quantum wire that occupies that same space as a single-qubit gate with label s would. The h version only occupies horizontal space, not vertical.

macros.name: linethrough
macros.doc: This command puts a quantum wire across the current cell.

macros.name: lstick
macros.doc: The basic commands for labelling wires at the start/end of a circuit are \lstick and \rstick respectively.

macros.name: makeebit
macros.doc: Create an e-bit. This places the label l halfway between the current row and the next row.

macros.name: octrl
macros.doc: Starting point of a controlled gate, using filled circle (\ctrl) or open circle (\octrl).

macros.name: phantomgate
macros.doc: Places a quantum wire that occupies that same space as a single-qubit gate with label s would.

macros.name: push
macros.doc: Places text t on the quantum wire, with no spacing or gate command around it.

macros.name: rstick
macros.doc: The basic commands for labelling wires at the start/end of a circuit are \lstick and \rstick respectively.

macros.name: setwiretype
macros.doc: Sets wire n (default: current row, from that column onwards) to being of type t, which must be one of: q (quantum), c (classical) or b (bundle).

macros.name: swap
macros.doc: Create an X shape on the current wire and a single vertical wire going downwards n rows (may be negative).

macros.name: wave
macros.doc: Draw a wave along an entire row. s is standard tikz formatting commands for additional control over the style.

macros.name: wire
macros.doc: Draw a wire starting from the current cell of type t which can be one of a (automatic), q, c, b, going in direction d (u,d,l,r for up/down/left/right) for a number of cells n. Automatic uses the current wire type of that wire.

macros.name: wireoverride
macros.doc: Sets the wire type for the current cell (i.e. the wire starting in this cell and going backwards) to t without changing the wire type for the rest of the row.
